title: GOP Campaign Cash Shifts From North Carolina to Kansas as Senate Map Changes
summary:
The biggest campaign spending group for Senate Republicans is moving money out of North Carolina and into Kansas. The shift shows how the party's effort to keep its Senate majority has become more defensive just a month before the midterm elections.

The Senate Leadership Fund is a super PAC, a political group that can raise and spend money to influence elections, and it is aligned with top Senate Republicans. Four people with direct knowledge of the decision disclosed it Friday, speaking anonymously to discuss internal strategy. The group will make a seven-figure advertising buy in Kansas and is pulling back in North Carolina.

The Associated Press reports that the move signals a lack of confidence that Michael Whatley, a former Republican National Committee chairman and Trump's choice for the Senate race in North Carolina, can beat Democratic former Gov. Roy Cooper. According to AdImpact, which tracks ad reservations, the fund had planned to spend $18 million in North Carolina over the next month. It has already spent about $32 million there.

Kansas is a state that Trump won by nearly 16 percentage points in the last presidential election. Sen. Roger Marshall, a Republican seeking a second term, won his first race in 2020 by more than 11 percentage points. Diesel costs and other economic concerns have made the state more competitive than Republicans expected, AP reports. Marshall faces Democratic nominee Adam Hamilton, the leader of the nation's largest United Methodist Church.

Republicans began this election cycle believing they had more chances to flip Democratic-held seats than they had incumbents at serious risk. Now they are spending money in states where Trump won comfortably in 2024.

Senate Republican campaign leaders have pointed to spiking fuel prices, driven in part by the war with Iran, as one issue weighing on their candidates. Trump said last month, while campaigning with Whatley, that higher fuel prices were "a very inexpensive price to pay" for preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon. Gas prices are near historic highs, but they remain below the nationwide record set in 2022.

The midterm elections on Nov. 3 will help determine control of Congress. The party that holds the Senate majority has more power to decide which bills and nominees move forward.
why_it_matters: Where a party spends its last campaign money shows which races it thinks are close, and the Senate majority helps decide which bills and nominees move forward.

questions.question: Who disclosed the Senate Leadership Fund's decision?
options: Michael Whatley in a TV interview
The group in a public press conference
Four people with direct knowledge, speaking anonymously
Roy Cooper's campaign team in a statement
questions.correct_answer: Four people with direct knowledge, speaking anonymously

questions.question: According to AdImpact, how much had the group planned to spend in North Carolina over the next month?
options: $16 million
$18 million
$32 million
$11 million

questions.question: What does the move signal, according to the Associated Press?
options: Doubt that Whatley can beat Cooper
Belief that North Carolina is already won
Anger that Cooper left the race
A plan to replace Whatley before Election Day
questions.correct_answer: Doubt that Whatley can beat Cooper

questions.question: What has helped make Kansas more competitive than Republicans expected?
options: A new candidate entering the race late
Diesel costs and other economic concerns
Fewer voters registering this year
A change in the state's voting laws
questions.correct_answer: Diesel costs and other economic concerns

questions.question: How did Republicans view the Senate map when this election cycle began?
options: They had more chances to flip seats than seats at risk
They hoped to run only in states Trump lost
They planned to avoid spending money on any ads
They expected to lose most of their Senate seats soon
questions.correct_answer: They had more chances to flip seats than seats at risk

questions.question: What did Trump say about higher fuel prices while campaigning with Whatley?
options: They would likely fall soon once the November election was over
They were a very inexpensive price to pay to stop Iran
They were mostly caused by diesel costs in Kansas farm country
They were not a topic that voters cared about at all
questions.correct_answer: They were a very inexpensive price to pay to stop Iran

background_read: A super PAC is an outside group. It can spend money to support candidates, but it is separate from the candidates' own campaigns.
Midterm elections take place halfway through a president's term and decide who sits in Congress.
